findings.message: Angular 12 is 10 majors behind 22 and out of support
findings.detail: Angular supports each major for 18 months, so only the newest three get fixes; 12 receives no security patches. `ng update` moves one major at a time, which makes this 10 sequential upgrade steps, each with its own migrations to review.

findings.message: 1 project still built with the webpack builder
findings.detail: The esbuild-based `application` builder has been the default since Angular 17 and builds several times faster. `ng update @angular/cli --name use-application-builder` migrates the configuration. Projects: ang2-conduit.
End of life since 2023. Replaced by Playwright or Cypress.
Deprecated since 2019. Replaced by ESLint with `angular-eslint`.
A set of TSLint rules, so it died with TSLint. Replaced by `angular-eslint`.

checks.title: Deprecated APIs
checks.summary: Nothing deprecated as of Angular 12 is in use; APIs deprecated in later versions surface at each upgrade step.

checks.title: Change detection & zoneless readiness
checks.summary: Runs on zone.js; 0% of 18 components use OnPush.

findings.message: Zoneless change detection needs Angular 20.2 or newer
findings.detail: Upgrade first; OnPush coverage is the preparation that pays off now.

Without `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` a component is checked on every change detection cycle and usually relies on zone.js to notice mutations. These are the components to review before going zoneless.

checks.title: Components & templates
checks.summary: 18 components: 0% standalone, 0% signal inputs, 0% built-in control flow.

findings.message: 18 components still declared in NgModules (16 NgModules in total)
findings.detail: Standalone components are the default since Angular 19 and what every new API assumes. `ng generate @angular/core:standalone` converts declarations, removes the emptied NgModules and switches bootstrapping, in three passes that can be reviewed one at a time.

Signal inputs (`input()`) make inputs readable in `computed()` and effects without `ngOnChanges`, and are what zoneless change detection tracks. `ng generate @angular/core:signal-input-migration` and `ng generate @angular/core:output-migration` convert most of them; the rest are usually inputs written to from inside the component.
Built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) is available from Angular 17. `ng generate @angular/core:control-flow` migrates most templates automatically.

checks.title: State management
checks.summary: No classic NgRx, 0 signal()/computed() calls, 0 signal-store files.

findings.detail: Each is a candidate for a `signal()`-based service: templates read it without the async pipe, `computed()` replaces `combineLatest` chains, and zoneless change detection tracks it automatically. `toObservable()` keeps existing RxJS consumers working during the move.

checks.title: Testing
checks.summary: Karma, 0 spec files, 0% of components and services with a spec.

findings.message: Unit tests run on Karma, which is deprecated
findings.detail: Karma was deprecated in 2023 and receives no further development. Vitest is the Angular CLI's default runner since v21 (`@angular/build:unit-test`). With no specs written yet, moving costs only the configuration, and the first specs can be written for Vitest directly.
32 component and service files without a single spec. Every refactoring and upgrade step is verified by hand.

findings.message: End-to-end tests use Protractor, which is end of life
findings.detail: Protractor reached end of life in 2023 and gets no fixes, including for new browser versions. Playwright and Cypress are the usual replacements.

checks.title: Type safety
checks.summary: strictNullChecks off, strictTemplates off, 13 explicit any.

findings.detail: Every value that may be `null` or `undefined` is typed as if it never is, so the most common runtime error in an Angular app is invisible to the compiler. In a large codebase switching it on is staged: a separate tsconfig that checks one folder at a time, with a count that may only go down.

Template bindings are only loosely type-checked: a wrong input type, a misspelled output payload or a possibly-undefined value passed to a component compiles and fails at runtime. Turning it on typically surfaces a batch of real bugs alongside the type noise.
An unannotated parameter silently becomes `any`, and no lint rule that counts the word `any` can see it.

findings.message: 13 explicit `any` in application code (8.1 per 1 000 lines)
findings.detail: Files with the most are listed first. Each `any` switches type checking off for everything that flows through it.
Each switches off checking for the next line, including errors nobody has seen yet.

checks.title: Circular dependencies
checks.summary: No import cycles between application files.
